children: Deal activity in biotech was selective this week but featured outsized transactions, anchored by Sanofi’s acquisition of Insmed, the largest deal in the sector for 2026, while Eli Lilly extended its buying streak.
Sanofi Agrees To Buy Insmed for $41B
Paris-based Sanofi (
) announced earlier this week an agreement to acquire rare disease drugmaker Insmed (INSM) for $175 per share in cash, equating to roughly $41 billion in equity value. The price represented about a

params.linkText: 46% premium to Insmed’s unaffected closing price on November 18

children: and roughly 17% above the prior day’s close.

The deal brings two commercial respiratory medicines under Sanofi—Brinsupri (brensocatib), the first approved therapy for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis, and Arikayce—plus the late-stage candidate treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP).

Sanofi said the transaction strengthens its immunology and rare-disease respiratory franchise as it prepares for future pressure on its blockbuster Regeneron-partnered drug Dupixent and is expected to be accretive to business earnings by the end of 2028. Closing is anticipated in the first half of 2027, subject to Insmed shareholder approval and regulatory clearances.

AbbVie’s acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics for approximately $10.9 billion, announced in June, was the largest pure biopharma company deal of 2026 before Sanofi-Insmed. Earlier this year, Sanofi completed the acquisition of Dynavax Technologies for about $2.2 billion in a bid to add the latter’s adult hepatitis B vaccine HEPLISAV-B to its portfolio and strengthen its adult immunization lineup.
Lilly Acquires Preclinical Huntington’s Developer LoQus23

American drugmaker Eli Lilly ( LLY), known for its obesity drug franchise, agreed this week to acquire UK-based and privately held LoQus23 Therapeutics for up to $725 million in cash. The amount includes an undisclosed upfront payment plus development and regulatory milestones.
LoQus23’s lead asset, LQT-23, is a preclinical drug expected to treat Huntington’s disease. The company expects to submit a clinical-trial application by year-end.

Eli Lilly has been the most active large-pharma acquirer in 2026, announcing roughly 11–12 company acquisitions with total potential value, including milestones, exceeding $25–32 billion and spanning oncology, immunology, neuroscience, vaccines, and rare diseases as it seeks to diversify its offerings and portfolio. Earlier this month, the company announced that it would buy Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion. In March, the company announced it would buy Centessa Pharmaceuticals for up to $7.8 billion.
How Did SNY And LLY Retail Traders React?
On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around SNY jumped from 'bullish' to 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while retail chatter rose from 'high' to 'extremely high' levels.
Meanwhile, sentiment around LLY jumped from 'bearish' to 'bullish' levels, accompanied by 'normal' message volume.
While SNY has added 10% year-to-date, LLY has added 30%.
